title: EU Storage at ~34% — Injection Season Underway but Pace Is Everything
hook: EU gas storage at 34.3%, well below 5-year average. To hit the 90% November mandate, Europe needs ~3,462 GWh/day injection rate. With Hormuz closed and TTF at €44, the economics are painful.
authorWord: The storage story hasn't changed: Europe starts injection from a deep hole. The question isn't whether we get to 90% — it's how much we pay to get there. Every week of delayed Hormuz reopening adds billions to the refill bill.
author: La Rédaction 🦊
details:
EU aggregate gas storage at approximately 34.3% full — significantly below the 5-year average for this time of year, per EnergyRiskIQ / AGSI+ data. At this fill rate, Europe must inject approximately 3,462 GWh/day on average to meet the EU-mandated 90% target by November 1. For context, the maximum theoretical daily injection capacity across all EU facilities is ~4,200 GWh/day — meaning there is very little margin for disruptions.

Injection season dynamics are challenging. The EU Gas Coordination Group confirmed in April that levels sit below the 5-year average but noted steady inflows since early April as a positive signal. However, several factors constrain the injection pace:

  • Price sensitivity: TTF at ~€44/MWh makes storage injection expensive vs the sub-€30 levels of 2023-24. Some market participants may delay injections hoping for lower prices.
  • LNG supply uncertainty: With Hormuz closed, ~20% of global LNG supply is stranded. Qatar's Ras Laffan — the world's largest LNG complex — remains under force majeure. Technip Energies is positioned to secure repair work, but Wood Mackenzie expects full service restoration only by end-August even if restarts begin in May.
  • Russian LNG spot ban: The EU's Russian LNG spot ban is now in effect as of April 25, per Bloomberg. Long-term contracts (~10-12 bcm/yr) are exempt, but spot volumes (~9 bcm/yr) that previously filled the gap are gone.

Country-level disparities: Germany (22% of EU storage capacity) typically leads injection pace but faces higher TTF prices. Italy, France, and the Netherlands also need aggressive fills. The Netherlands has benefited from Groningen field flexibility, but that resource is being wound down.

Bruegel data visualization shows the daily change in storage fullness over the last 30 days: the required injection rate is +0.25 percentage points per day to meet the mandatory 80% interim target, let alone 90% by November 1.

💡 Trade Ideas

1. Long TTF Calendar Spread — Buy Dec 2026 / Sell Jun 2026: The winter 2026/27 contract must price in refill risk. If injection pace falls behind (likely given Hormuz constraints), the Dec-Jun spread widens from current ~€0 to €5-10. Buy Dec '26 TTF, sell Jun '26 TTF. This is the canonical storage-fill trade.

2. Long TTF Summer '26 Volatility: Any disruption to injection (heatwave reducing sendout, LNG cargo delays, geopolitical escalation) would spike near-dated TTF. Summer 2026 implied vol is likely underpriced given the binary outcomes on Hormuz. Buy Jun or Jul TTF straddles.

3. Storage Arbitrage — Fixed-Price Injection Strip: For physical players: lock in TTF summer '26 prices (~€43-44/MWh) for injection volumes now. If TTF spikes in Q3 on Hormuz news, the spread between fixed injection cost and spot winter price widens. Essentially a synthetic physical storage play via financial contracts.

⚡ Dissenting View — Dante 🔥
34% is the number everyone quotes, but the key metric is GWh injected per day vs target. We're probably running at ~2,800-3,000 GWh/day right now — below the 3,462 needed. Every week we're behind adds ~10 TWh to the deficit. By August, if Hormuz is still closed, we'll need 4,000+ GWh/day — which is near max capacity. One pipeline outage, one LNG terminal problem, and we miss the target. The market is not pricing this tail risk correctly.
